1. MarginPad — best overall, and the only one that pays you

BEST FOR: almost everyone learning futures

Opens in the browser with no sign-up, fills at live exchange prices on 60+ crypto perps plus US stocks, forex, indices and gold, and simulates the real thing: leverage to 1000x, isolated-margin liquidation, funding, stop-loss/take-profit, partial closes, a trade journal. The unique part: practice earns real USDT — weekly leaderboards pay top traders and daily missions pay for using the tools. There is also a full social layer (chat, duels, follows) and a free Academy.

Honest cons: no bot backtesting like Gainium/WunderTrading, no multi-year history archives, and the social/rewards layer needs a (free) account.

2. TradingView Paper Trading — best if you live in its charts

BEST FOR: chartists already on TradingView

Unbeatable charting with a paper account built in, across every asset class. If your entire workflow is TradingView drawings and indicators, practicing where you chart is a real advantage.

Honest cons: requires an account, and its own docs note paper trading does not simulate perpetual settlement, funding fees or realistic liquidation — the exact mechanics that blow up real futures accounts. See our full TradingView comparison.

3. Binance Futures Testnet — best for Binance's exact interface

BEST FOR: traders planning to trade on Binance specifically

A faithful replica of Binance Futures with test funds — the real UI, order types and margin modes you would use live on Binance.

Honest cons: needs an account, the test balance is small, and it runs an isolated order book — fills can print at prices the live market never traded, which distorts practice. See our Binance testnet comparison.

4. Bybit Demo Trading — best exchange-native demo

BEST FOR: future Bybit traders

Live prices in Bybit's real interface with demo funds, including perps mechanics. The most realistic of the exchange demos.

Honest cons: requires a Bybit account (a funnel toward depositing), crypto only, and no journal/social/rewards layer.

5. Gainium — best for bot strategy testing

BEST FOR: bot traders

Paper trading built into a bot platform: test DCA/grid strategies against live prices before running them with money. Polished product and generous free tier.

Honest cons: account required, bot-first (manual practice is secondary), crypto only.

6. WunderTrading — best bot-platform alternative

BEST FOR: bot traders comparing options

Similar shape to Gainium: demo trading inside an automation platform, live prices, good for validating automated strategies.

Honest cons: same trade-offs — account required, automation-first, crypto only.

7. CryptoParrot — simplest game-style practice

BEST FOR: absolute beginners who want zero pressure

A friendly, game-like simulator with a community feel — the gentlest possible introduction to placing trades.

Honest cons: spot-style trading without real perps mechanics, so it will not teach you leverage, funding or liquidation.
